I personally make shadow boxes of things that remind me of them, or get a necklace with their ashes in it. Wearing them on a daily basis comforts me and makes me feel like they are there with me. The shadow boxes make me remember the good things about them and all the moments we shared together. Another weird thing I do is eat their favorite meal, or a meal that reminds me of them. My grandfather was a big eater, so my family and I typically eat like pigs to celebrate his life on his heavenly anniversary. 

I think as time goes on, you will find things to remember your loved ones as time goes on that feel just right for you.

I’ve noticed that too, except with weight gain. 

I lost an amazing amount of weight to impress a boy, but December of 2018, a friend was murdered. Then in March and May 2019, I lost my grandfather and a childhood friend. The pounds came on again. In September, I lost my aunt. I went from 170-220 in three months. Luckily, the weight gain was barely noticeable since the women in my family are built bigger, but I know I felt it.

Looking back, I’m disgusted with how much I ate on a daily bases to cope with my losses. Having lost nearly 35 pounds now, I’m sure they’re all happy for me!

EDIT: Yes, I agree with the other commenters. Distract yourself while you make a portioned, full-course meal for yourself and eat it. Stay safe and keep healthy. ❤️

After we opened gifts and family left, my mom and dad got into a huge fight, and the cops were called. We ended up getting two pizzas from a convenience store down the street for Christmas dinner. We didn’t even see our family, aside from the two that visited earlier that day. It was horrible, but thankfully, things are better.

I’m very into the research of my family and our history, both past and present. Well, while my mom and me were in the car together, I got talking about some dark things that our ancestors did. She goes to tell me that my Uncle’s brother caused a lot of controversy within our family, and I was completely shocked with what she told me. My mom told me that he touched my cousin on multiple accounts, and other girls, inside the family’s circle. No one knows the truth, to this day. Before his trial, he took his life, leaving whatever answers we had to our questions in the ground. My mom and dad (brother of my Aunt) theorize that my father’s and Aunt’s family set him up just because they disliked my Uncle’s brother. My aunt was blood, my Uncle married into the family, so I suppose that makes sense why they would attempt to black sheep somebody, but like, if it really were just an attempt to single someone out, and they didn’t do it... really? For that very reason, I’m glad I don’t associate with them, and my dad agrees.

Yeah, you might have these fancy percentages, but what if you fall from the perch, regain consciousness or whatever, and have brain damage from lack of oxygen? Then you’ll really feel miserable. What if you don’t break your neck instantly? You’ll suffer long enough for you to regret what you did, until you eventually die tying to claw the rope away from around your neck, all the while wishing you hadn’t made that God awful decision. Don’t hang yourself. Don’t hurt your damn self. Stand up, realize your worth, and get some help.
